oewn-08002390-n.learner: All the people who are in a room.
examples: When he told the joke, the whole room laughed.

oewn-08014145-n.learner: A group of things that all have something in common.
examples: English and German belong to the same family of languages.

oewn-08124465-n.learner: In biology, a group of living things that is made up of one or more smaller groups called genera.
examples: Lions, tigers and house cats all belong to the cat family.

oewn-10256001-n.learner: A person who is related to you or to other people.
examples: You don't need to knock; you're family.

oewn-08244837-n.learner: A group of people who share the same beliefs or do the same things together.
examples: Everyone who works or studies here is part of the school family.

oewn-08263223-n.learner: a loose group of gangsters who together run organized crime.
examples: The police arrested three members of a powerful crime family.

connotation.why: calls a criminal gang by the warm word for kin, against plain 'syndicate'

oewn-10101225-n.learner: A person who has an important or highly respected position in an organization.
examples: The city fathers met to decide where the new bridge should go.

oewn-10045020-n.learner: The leader of an organized crime family.
examples: Every member of the gang obeyed the father without question.

oewn-01828474-v.learner: To feel or say a hope about what will happen to someone or how their life will go.
examples: Although they had quarrelled, she still wished him well.

oewn-00904886-v.learner: To say words that call something, such as a good night or good luck, down on someone.
examples: She wished everyone good night and went upstairs.

oewn-00786389-v.learner: To put a question in order to get an answer to it.
examples: The teacher asked a question that nobody could answer.

oewn-00757790-v.learner: To think of something as required, or to ask for something and expect to get it.
examples: All I ask of you is that you tell the truth.

oewn-01070587-v.learner: To want a certain price or condition in return for something.
examples: He is asking two hundred pounds for the horse.

oewn-02492311-v.learner: To invite someone to go out with you on a date.
examples: He finally asked her out to the dance on Friday.

oewn-02492581-v.learner: To come together with other people to spend time or to do something.
examples: We met for coffee to talk about the plan.

oewn-01185870-v.learner: To do or have what a need, wish, rule, or limit calls for.
examples: Her work did not meet the standard the school expected.

oewn-02745355-v.learner: To get a certain response from other people.
examples: His plan met with little support.

oewn-02716276-v.learner: To be next to each other, or to come together at one point.
examples: The two roads meet just outside the village.

oewn-01208316-v.learner: To touch something directly, or to come into touch with it.
examples: The glass met the stone floor with a crash.

oewn-02433771-v.learner: To gather together in one place.
examples: A large crowd met in the square before the march.

oewn-01081873-v.learner: To play or fight against someone in a sport, a game, or a battle.
examples: The two teams will meet in the final.

oewn-02114536-v.learner: To go through something, or to suffer it.
examples: The ship met a terrible end in the storm.

oewn-07340708-n.learner: The earliest part or time of something.
examples: In the morning of life, everything seems possible.
The chairman began the meeting with a short speech.

oewn-02532175-v.learner: To do even a very small part of something, usually said with 'not'.
examples: I can't begin to thank you for all your help.

oewn-02614382-v.learner: To have a starting point in time, in space, or on a scale.
examples: The path begins at the church gate.
Prices begin at ten pounds.

oewn-02614858-v.learner: To start in a particular way.
examples: The day began badly, with rain and a missed coach.

oewn-02685037-v.learner: To be the first thing or point in a series.
examples: The letter A begins the alphabet.

oewn-02606945-v.learner: To start the activity that an object is meant for, such as starting to read a book or smoke a cigar.
examples: He began a new book last night.

oewn-01072799-v.learner: To start to speak, understand, read, and write a language.
examples: She began Spanish when she was seven.

oewn-02697056-v.learner: To be in a certain place.
examples: The old house sits on top of a hill.

oewn-02028720-v.learner: To be holding an official meeting.
examples: Parliament will not sit again until September.

oewn-01546780-v.learner: To lead someone to a seat, or to give someone a seat.
examples: The waiter sat us at a table by the window.

oewn-01097992-v.learner: To serve in a particular professional or official role.
examples: He sits on the board of the bank.

oewn-02147248-v.learner: To hold a position, for example so that an artist can paint or draw you.
examples: She sat for the painter every morning for a month.

oewn-01961388-v.learner: To sit on an animal's back and travel on it, usually while guiding how it moves.
examples: He sits a horse better than anyone in the county.

oewn-02461692-v.learner: To work or act as a babysitter.
examples: I can sit for the neighbours' children on Saturday.

oewn-08255581-n.learner: A group of students who finish their studies at the same time.
examples: The whole year went on the trip to London.
